value.quote: We report the results of an experimental voting game
value.note: Section 2 derives equilibria (NE, SPE). Section 4 and the appendices report laboratory experiments, which make up most of the results.

C1.reason: The strategic voting here is analysed only through equilibrium (EQ) and experiments (EM); there is no separate manipulation or strategyproofness analysis that would justify adding SB.

value.quote_info: All players’ signs and cost/benefit ratios are common knowledge.
value.note: In the experiment, the strategy method left some uncertainty about predecessors' identities (footnote 11).

C6.VOT.reason: No analysis fixes voters' actions by the model, since experimental subjects choose freely and heuristics are only used to explain deviations, so STRAT fits better than MIXED.

value.quote: sequential voting has a unique subgame perfect equilibrium
value.note: Dominant strategies are applied to non-critical voters. Pure and mixed Nash equilibria are used for simultaneous voting. A bounded-rationality approach is used to explain deviations.

C8.1.reason: The model explicitly uses dominant strategies to remove non-critical voters ('i has the dominant strategy to vote Yes'), so DOM belongs alongside NE, SPE and BND.
